# 少样本图像分类中度量学习方法的比较：问题与综述范围

## 摘要

本报告比较面向少样本图像分类的度量学习方法：它们共同学习特征嵌入和/或相似性度量，并依据查询样本与支持样本的距离分类，而非在少量样本上训练复杂分类器。按推理链条可分为改进特征嵌入、类别表示和距离度量三类；代表性路线包括 K-tuplet 与 triplet/ICNN 几何约束、关系网络的可学习非线性比较、SRL 的子空间表示、MSENet 的多层级融合，以及不确定性感知的相似性建模。现有论文分别在 miniImageNet、TieredImageNet、CUB、FC100 或跨域任务中报告竞争力、改进或当时最先进性能；但除 Proto-Triplet/ICNN 在 miniImageNet 摘要中报告约 2 个百分点相对提升外，冻结材料缺少共享 backbone、shot 设置和完整数值，不能形成统一准确率排名。 [E:arxiv:2105.08149:page:1:block:9:claim:7cf2d36a262c] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] [E:arxiv:2105.08149:abstract:claim:ae8bdfee0e05] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:4:b851ec357ca4:claim:3868df819471] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6]

## 引言

少样本图像分类要解决的核心问题是：在每个新类别只有少量标注样本的条件下，模型仍需识别未见过的视觉概念；这一设定使深度网络容易因样本稀少而过拟合。度量学习路线通过学习特征嵌入和/或距离（或相似性）度量，把未见样本按照其与已见支持样本的距离进行分类，从而避免直接在少量样本上训练复杂分类器。 [E:arxiv:2105.08149:page:1:block:9:claim:7cf2d36a262c]

本综述的比较对象限定为面向少样本图像分类的度量学习方法，重点不是一般的迁移学习或所有元学习方法：迁移学习通常先在 ImageNet 等上游数据集预训练，再在下游任务上微调；元学习则在许多不同分类任务上训练元学习器以获得可快速迁移的知识。度量学习可以借助 episodic 的支持集—查询集训练，但评价时应关注其表征、类别表示和距离函数如何共同决定泛化性能。 [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:2:c92e388de5e0:claim:a5140904b8b9] [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:2:c92e388de5e0:claim:1a6b9a5336b7] [E:arxiv:2105.08149:page:1:block:9:claim:70e47785f750]

在典型的基于度量的少样本流程中，查询样本根据特征相似性寻找支持集中最近的原型或类别表示；因此，方法差异主要体现在嵌入空间如何学习、少量支持样本如何聚合成类别表示，以及相似性比较是固定的还是可学习的。已有综述将 2018–2022 年的深度度量学习方法按这三个阶段划分为学习特征嵌入、学习类别表示和学习距离度量三类。 [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] [E:arxiv:2105.08149:abstract:claim:ae8bdfee0e05]

本报告将沿上述分类比较代表性方法的机制与证据，包括通过 K-tuplet 或 triplet 类损失强化嵌入关系、用可学习关系网络替代固定欧氏度量、以子空间表示保留空间结构，以及用多层级特征或不确定性建模改进比较；实验部分只在数据集、任务设置（如 5-way 1-shot/5-shot）和评价指标可对照时比较结果，跨数据集或训练协议不同的结论将明确标注为不能直接排名。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596]

## 基础概念与方法分类

分类的第一层级先区分学习范式，而不是把所有少样本方法都归为度量学习：来源将少样本学习概括为迁移学习与元学习两大类别；迁移学习先在 ImageNet 等上游数据上预训练，再适配下游任务，元学习则通过许多不同任务获得可迁移的学习能力。 [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:2:c92e388de5e0:claim:a5140904b8b9] [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:2:c92e388de5e0:claim:1a6b9a5336b7] [E:arxiv:2105.08149:page:1:block:9:claim:70e47785f750] 本综述所称度量学习是元学习/少样本框架内的一条技术路线，其共同判据是学习特征嵌入和/或距离或相似性度量，并依据未见查询样本与已见支持样本之间的距离完成分类；因此，单纯依赖大规模上游预训练和下游微调的迁移学习基线不应仅凭也能完成少样本任务而被归入同一机制类别。 [E:arxiv:2105.08149:page:1:block:9:claim:7cf2d36a262c] [E:arxiv:2105.08149:page:1:block:9:claim:e0be331540fc]

在度量学习内部，可按推理链条的三个阶段分类：学习特征嵌入、学习类别表示、学习距离度量；这一标准来自一篇覆盖 2018–2022 年深度度量学习少样本图像分类方法的综述，优势是能把“样本怎样编码”“支持集怎样形成类原型”“查询与类别怎样比较”分开分析。 [E:arxiv:2105.08149:abstract:claim:ae8bdfee0e05] 第一类标准关注嵌入函数本身：若方法的主要贡献是利用样本间关系、类内/类间距离或多层级特征来改善特征空间，使其对未见类别更可分，应归入特征嵌入改进；例如 K-tuplet 网络强调训练样本关系，Proto-Triplet 与 ICNN 损失显式约束类内和类间距离，MSENet 则从不同网络阶段抽取多输出特征。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] 第二类标准关注支持集如何形成类别表示：最近原型方法把查询样本与支持集原型的特征相似性作为分类依据，而子空间表示学习把传统向量表示扩展为局部 CNN 特征空间中的子空间，并用 prototypical subspace 或 discriminative subspace 聚合 K-shot 信息；二者的关键差异在类别表示是单个向量/原型，还是能保留空间结构与类内多样性的子空间。 [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] 第三类标准关注比较函数是否固定：传统度量学习方法通常学习可迁移嵌入但预先规定欧氏等固定度量，而关系网络训练网络执行类别间比较，提供可学习而非固定、非线性而非线性的判别关系；这使“距离度量学习”区别于仅改进嵌入或原型的方法。 [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:4:b851ec357ca4:claim:3868df819471] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64]

这些类别是互补关系而非互斥排名：一个方法可能同时改进嵌入和距离，例如 K-tuplet 表征可与非线性距离函数结合，多层级嵌入网络也可用可学习阶段权重；因此后续比较应分别说明各方法作用于哪个阶段，而不能把架构复杂度、 episodic 训练形式或跨域测试结果直接等同于准确率排名。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:5a36249bbf1e] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] 还需区分任务目标与效率目标：本分类回答的是少样本图像分类中度量信息如何被学习和使用；来源中的大规模迁移学习与 Meta-Dataset 评估用于揭示 episodic 方法和迁移学习各自的适用边界，属于不同范式的外部对照，并不提供可插入度量学习三阶段分类的距离函数，也不能在训练协议不匹配时支持方法间的直接优劣排序。 [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:3fb7cfd2fbdb] [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:1453b845fef7]

## 代表性方法分析

深度 K-tuplet 网络的机制出发点是把经典深度度量学习中的 triplet network 扩展为 K-tuplet network，并通过 episodic training 同时利用一个输入样本组内多个训练样本之间的关系；其贡献在于把少样本学习的重点从单纯的查询—支持相似度比较转向更有判别力的通用特征嵌入。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] 该方法训练后可对未见过的新类别提取判别性特征；来源还说明该特征提取器可以与非线性距离度量函数结合，因此其适用边界首先是作为表征学习模块，而不是单独证明某一种固定距离函数必然最优。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:5a36249bbf1e] 深度 K-tuplet 方法的证据包括在 miniImageNet 上超过其他基于度量的少样本分类方法，以及在以 miniImageNet 训练后迁移到 Caltech-101、CUB-200、Stanford Dogs 和 Stanford Cars 时显著超过先前方法；这些结果支持其跨未见类别的泛化能力，但具体数值、任务 shot 设置和基线条件需在实验章节按原报告核对后才能排名。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:b4d49aba47c5]

Proto-Triplet Loss 与 ICNN Loss 的共同机制是直接约束嵌入向量的几何结构：前者由原始 triplet loss 修改而来以适应少样本情景，后者依据类内与类间最近邻分数评估嵌入质量；二者都显式处理少量数据中的类内距离和类间距离，而不是只依赖末端分类误差。 [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] 这一路线的贡献在于把潜在空间中不同类别的可分性作为训练目标，来源报告其在 miniImageNet 上相对其他基于度量的少样本方法获得约 2 个百分点的准确率提升，并称其能更好泛化到先前未见类别；该 2% 是摘要给出的相对改进幅度，不能脱离被比较方法和实验协议解释为所有设置下的固定增益。 [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] 同一损失函数研究还在 Caltech CUB、Dogs 和 Cars 等其他域上报告了与当时最先进方法相竞争的泛化能力；因此其适用范围不限于 miniImageNet 内部分类，但“competitive”表示相对比较结论，来源摘要没有在当前材料中给出可逐项排序的全部数值。 [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:aaed703eb739]

关系网络（Relation Network）类方法的核心机制是训练一个网络来执行类别之间的比较，而不是在学习到嵌入后使用静态度量；在少样本任务中，这使网络能够根据当前比较决定各类别哪些方面更重要，并用数据驱动的关系模块生成相似性判断。 [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] 相对于主要学习可迁移嵌入并预先规定欧氏等固定度量的方法，关系网络提供的是可学习而非固定、非线性而非线性的分类关系；其方法贡献位于距离度量或相似性函数阶段，适合与固定欧氏距离或线性分类器形成机制对照。 [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:4:b851ec357ca4:claim:3868df819471] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] 关系网络的证据是其灵活架构在实践中表现良好，并在 Caltech-UCSD Birds 细粒度分类任务上达到当时的最先进性能；这一证据特别指向细粒度鸟类分类，不能仅凭机制推广为在 miniImageNet、跨域或不同 backbone 下普遍优于其他度量学习方法。 [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64]

子空间表示学习（SRL）把每张图像表示为局部 CNN 特征空间中的一个子空间，并使用加权子空间距离（WSD）度量两幅图像的相似性；这一机制把传统基于向量的度量学习扩展到基于子空间的表示与比较。 [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] 当每个类别有 K 张图像时，SRL 设计了 prototypical subspace（PS）和 discriminative subspace（DS）两类模板子空间来聚合 K-shot 信息；相对于全局向量原型，其主要机制收益是保留图像内部的空间结构以及图像或类别内的多样性。 [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] SRL 的实验证据来自 MiniImageNet、TieredImageNet 和 CUB 三个公开基准，结果显示该框架相对于先前最先进方法具有竞争力或更优；该结论支持子空间表示在这些基准上的有效性，但“competitive/superior”仍需结合具体 1-shot/5-shot 指标和基线，不能抽象成统一排名。 [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6]

MSENet 的机制是使用多输出嵌入网络，把样本映射到不同特征空间，并从网络不同阶段提取特征向量；来源认为浅层特征也包含对少样本分类有用的信息，而传统度量方法常只依赖查询特征与支持特征之间的单一距离值，因而可能忽略这些层级信息。 [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] MSENet 在每个阶段结合自注意力以精炼特征，并为不同阶段分配可学习权重；其机制目标是同时获得全局、抽象以及较早层的表征，再由多空间特征融合提升少样本分类性能。 [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] MSENet 的评估覆盖 MiniImageNet 和 FC100 的 5-way 1-shot、5-way 5-shot 情景，以及跨八个基准数据集的跨域任务；来源称其相对最先进方法有效并在测试域取得高准确率，但当前材料只提供摘要层面的结论，缺少可直接写入精确排名的准确率表。 [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f]

不确定性感知少样本框架针对的是度量学习中的相似性可靠性问题：神经网络对不同查询—支持对计算出的相似性具有不同不确定性，该方法把观察到的相似性转换为概率表示，并将其纳入损失以进行不确定性感知优化。 [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] 为了联合考虑一个查询与支持集中多个原型之间的相似性，该框架使用图模型估计各查询—支持对的不确定性；其贡献不是重新定义单个静态距离，而是在原型最近邻分类流程上增加对相似性噪声和关系结构的建模。 [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] 该框架的来源证据是在强基线基础上带来显著改进并达到最先进性能；不过当前可用文本没有给出数据集、任务设置或准确率数值，因此这里只能确认其机制和作者报告的改进方向，具体实验优劣必须等待可核对的结果表后再比较。 [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f]

## 综合比较与证据分析

实验比较首先按可核对的评价协议分组，而不是把所有论文摘要中的“state-of-the-art”合并成总排名：现有材料明确给出的共同任务形式主要是少样本基准上的准确率比较，但多数来源没有在摘要中同时提供 backbone、训练轮数、episode 构造、置信区间和完整数值，因此只能比较作者报告的数据集、shot 设置和相对结论。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] 在 miniImageNet 单一基准上，深度 K-tuplet 网络被报告优于其他基于度量的少样本分类方法；Proto-Triplet Loss 与 ICNN Loss 被报告相对其他基于度量的方法带来约 2 个百分点的准确率提升。二者都以 miniImageNet 为评价基准并声称优于度量学习对照方法，但当前材料没有给出彼此的共同基线、具体 1-shot/5-shot 数值或同一训练配置，因此不能判定 K-tuplet 与这两种损失哪一个更高。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] 跨域泛化实验中，深度 K-tuplet 网络使用 miniImageNet 训练后，在 Caltech-101、CUB-200、Stanford Dogs 和 Stanford Cars 四个数据集上被报告显著优于先前方法；Proto-Triplet/ICNN 研究则只报告在 Caltech CUB、Dogs 和 Cars 上与当时最先进方法相竞争。二者测试域有重叠但结论强度不同，且来源未提供统一数值和协议，故只能说明 K-tuplet 摘要声称“显著优于”、损失函数方法声称“有竞争力”，不能据此构造精确跨域排名。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:b4d49aba47c5] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:aaed703eb739] SRL 框架的实验范围是 MiniImageNet、TieredImageNet 和 CUB 三个公开基准，作者报告其相对于先前最先进方法具有竞争力或更优；该结论覆盖的数据集与 K-tuplet 的 miniImageNet 及跨域测试部分重叠，但 SRL 摘要没有给出各基准 1-shot/5-shot 的准确率数值，K-tuplet 摘要也未给出可逐项对照的表格，因此二者只能在“作者报告的相对表现”层面并置，不能直接比较百分点差异。 [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:b4d49aba47c5] MSENet 的实验设置在当前材料中最明确：它在 MiniImageNet 和 FC100 上评估 ## 局限与开放问题

当前证据最直接暴露的开放问题是评价协议不可直接合并：把 Meta-Dataset 协议用于大规模数据和大容量迁移学习器时，研究同时观察到 episodic 方法的局限以及迁移学习自身不足的方面；这说明少样本性能不能只由“是否采用 episodic 训练”或“是否使用大规模预训练”来解释。 [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:3fb7cfd2fbdb] 这一限制对度量学习比较的含义是，K-tuplet、关系网络、SRL、MSENet 或损失函数方法若采用不同的 episodic 任务、上游数据和模型容量，就不能把各自论文中的最先进结论合并为统一排行榜；Meta-Dataset 研究提供的是范式边界证据，而不是这些度量方法在同一设置下的相互数值对照。 [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:3fb7cfd2fbdb] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596]

固定距离函数构成第二类机制性约束：传统度量学习方法通常把学习重点放在可迁移嵌入上，并预先规定欧氏等固定度量；当类别比较需要随任务或查询样本改变关注的特征方面时，静态度量无法自主决定哪些类别属性对当前比较更重要。 [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:4:b851ec357ca4:claim:3868df819471] [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] 关系网络通过训练网络执行类别间比较来缓解这一约束，并提供可学习而非固定、非线性而非线性的关系；但来源证据主要是其在 Caltech-UCSD Birds 细粒度任务上表现良好并达到当时最先进水平，因此不能把该机制优势外推为所有数据集、shot 设置或 backbone 下的普遍优势。 [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996]

嵌入空间几何约束也存在适用条件：Proto-Triplet Loss 与 ICNN Loss 分别通过修改 triplet loss、计算类内和类间最近邻分数来增强潜在空间可分性；摘要报告其在 miniImageNet 上相对其他基于度量的方法约有 2 个百分点准确率提升。 [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] 该约 2% 增益是相对于摘要所指的其他基于度量的少样本方法，并依赖相应 miniImageNet 实验设置；在缺少共同基线、shot 数、backbone 和完整结果表时，不能把它解释为对关系网络、SRL、MSENet 或 K-tuplet 的统一领先幅度。 [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24]

子空间表示的取舍在于表示能力与比较形式的改变：SRL 用局部 CNN 特征空间中的子空间表示图像，并以加权子空间距离比较相似性，从而把向量度量学习扩展到子空间；其 PS 与 DS 模板旨在聚合 K-shot 信息并保留空间结构和类内多样性。 [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] 这种设计可能优于把图像压缩成全局向量的做法，但来源只在 MiniImageNet、TieredImageNet 和 CUB 上报告相对先前最先进方法具有竞争力或更优；当前材料没有给出子空间构造、维度选择、计算开销或各 shot 设置的完整数值，因此不能进一步断言其在效率和准确率上同时占优。 [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6]

多层级与不确定性方法反映了另一个共同问题：单一距离或单一相似性可能不足以表达少样本比较。MSENet 针对传统方法只依赖查询特征与支持特征之间单一距离、忽略浅层特征的问题，引入多输出空间、自注意力和可学习阶段权重；不确定性框架则把不同查询—支持对相似性的不确定性纳入概率表示和损失。 [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] 这两类方法增加了信息来源或可靠性建模，但给定来源只支持有限结论：MSENet 的摘要报告在 MiniImageNet、FC100 的 5-way 1-shot/5-shot 以及八个跨域基准上有效，却未提供精确准确率；不确定性框架摘要也未给出数据集、任务设置和数值，因而不能据架构模块更多推断其准确率、延迟或参数量必然更优。 [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f]

跨域证据同样需要谨慎解释。K-tuplet 网络在以 miniImageNet 训练后，于 Caltech-101、CUB-200、Stanford Dogs 和 Stanford Cars 上被报告显著优于先前方法；Proto-Triplet/ICNN 则在 Caltech CUB、Dogs 和 Cars 上报告与最先进方法相竞争。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:b4d49aba47c5] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:aaed703eb739] 这些结果支持研究者关于未见类别或其他域泛化的主张，但测试集合并不完全相同，结论强度也分别为“显著优于”和“有竞争力”；在没有统一域划分、shot 协议、准确率数值和统计显著性信息时，不能判定哪一种嵌入几何策略具有普遍更好的跨域迁移能力。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:b4d49aba47c5] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:aaed703eb739]

总体而言，来源支持的开放问题不是缺少某一种单一技巧，而是度量学习三阶段之间存在条件化权衡：更强嵌入可改善可分性，可学习关系可提高比较灵活性，子空间和多层级特征可保留结构与层级信息，不确定性建模可处理相似性可靠性；但这些收益均绑定各自基准和协议。 [E:arxiv:2105.08149:abstract:claim:ae8bdfee0e05] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] 因此，后续若要形成可靠排名，需要在同一 backbone、训练数据、episode 构造、5-way shot 设置、评价指标和统计口径下复测这些方法；现有冻结来源没有提供这种全覆盖的共享实验表，故本综述只能保留条件化比较，而不能填补数值或提出未经来源支持的全域结论。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:3fb7cfd2fbdb]

## 结论

结论上，度量学习方法的主要取舍发生在三个互补阶段：嵌入方法改善未见类别的可分性，子空间或原型决定支持集信息如何聚合，固定欧氏度量与可学习关系模块决定比较的灵活性。K-tuplet 和几何损失侧重嵌入，关系网络侧重非线性比较，SRL 保留空间结构与类内多样性，MSENet 利用多层级特征，不确定性框架处理相似性可靠性；这些机制位置本身不能证明准确率、速度或参数量优势。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:4:b851ec357ca4:claim:3868df819471] [E:arxiv:1711.06025:section:abstract:12:43376954155c:claim:71df1568e996] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] [E:arxiv:2105.08149:abstract:claim:ae8bdfee0e05]

可支持的答案是条件化比较：各方法在作者报告的基准和协议内相对相应基线有效或具有竞争力，但跨数据集、训练协议、shot 数、backbone 和结果表不匹配时不能直接排序。尤其是 CUB、miniImageNet 跨域和 Meta-Dataset/迁移学习证据只能说明范式边界或局部表现；若要可靠回答何者更优，需要在同一 5-way 1-shot/5-shot 设置、训练数据、模型容量、评价指标和统计口径下复测。 [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:998fb93b2a24] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72c0d6] [E:arxiv:2409.07989:abstract:claim:5ed923dac68f] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167d596] [E:arxiv:1907.03123:abstract:claim:b4d49aba47c5] [E:arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:aaed703eb739] [E:arxiv:1802.04376:abstract:claim:50a611de7d64] [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:3fb7cfd2fbdb] [E:arxiv:2104.02638:section:abstract:9:1354132472a1:claim:1453b845fef7] [E:arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4f03f] [E:arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:38498384e907]

arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167.claim_text: Using the two proposed loss functions, the few-shot learning method achieves a 2% accuracy improvement on the miniImageNet benchmark compared to other metric-based few-shot learning methods, demonstrating better generalization to previously unseen classes.
arxiv:2305.09062:abstract:claim:549b9167.supporting_text: Few-shot learning is a challenging area of research that aims to learn new concepts with only a few labeled samples of data. Recent works based on metric-learning approaches leverage the meta-learning approach, which is encompassed by episodic tasks that make use a support (training) and query set (test) with the objective of learning a similarity comparison metric between those sets. Due to the lack of data, the learning process of the embedding network becomes an important part of the few-shot task. Previous works have addressed this problem using metric learning approaches, but the properties of the underlying latent space and the separability of the difference classes on it was not entirely enforced. In this work, we propose two different loss functions which consider the importance of the embedding vectors by looking at the intra-class and inter-class distance between the few data. The first loss function is the Proto-Triplet Loss, which is based on the original triplet loss with the modifications needed to better work on few-shot scenarios. The second loss function, which we dub ICNN loss is based on an inter and intra class nearest neighbors score, which help us to assess the quality of embeddings obtained from the trained network. Our results, obtained from a extensive experimental setup show a significant improvement in accuracy in the miniImagenNet benchmark compared to other metric-based few-shot learning methods by a margin of 2%, demonstrating the capability of these loss functions to allow the network to generalize better to previously unseen classes. In our experiments, we demonstrate competitive generalization capabilities to other domains, such as the Caltech CUB, Dogs and Cars datasets compared with the state of the art.

arxiv:2105.08149:abstract:claim:ae8bdfee.supporting_text: Few-shot image classification is a challenging problem that aims to achieve the human level of recognition based only on a small number of training images. One main solution to few-shot image classification is deep metric learning. These methods, by classifying unseen samples according to their distances to few seen samples in an embedding space learned by powerful deep neural networks, can avoid overfitting to few training images in few-shot image classification and have achieved the state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we provide an up-to-date review of deep metric learning methods for few-shot image classification from 2018 to 2022 and categorize them into three groups according to three stages of metric learning, namely learning feature embeddings, learning class representations, and learning distance measures. arxiv:2105.00379:abstract:claim:e2d40a72.supporting_text: In this paper, we propose a subspace representation learning (SRL) framework to tackle few-shot image classification tasks. It exploits a subspace in local CNN feature space to represent an image, and measures the similarity between two images according to a weighted subspace distance (WSD). When K images are available for each class, we develop two types of template subspaces to aggregate K-shot information: the prototypical subspace (PS) and the discriminative subspace (DS). Based on the SRL framework, we extend metric learning based techniques from vector to subspace representation. While most previous works adopted global vector representation, using subspace representation can effectively preserve the spatial structure, and diversity within an image. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the SRL framework on three public benchmark datasets: MiniImageNet, TieredImageNet and Caltech-UCSD Birds-200-2011 (CUB), and the experimental results illustrate competitive/superior performance of our method compared to the previous state-of-the-art.

We also deviate from traditional metric-learning approaches by training a network to perform comparisons between classes rather than relying on a static metric comparison. arxiv:2010.04525:abstract:claim:7178a9c4.supporting_text: Few-shot image classification learns to recognize new categories from limited labelled data. Metric learning based approaches have been widely investigated, where a query sample is classified by finding the nearest prototype from the support set based on their feature similarities. A neural network has different uncertainties on its calculated similarities of different pairs. Understanding and modeling the uncertainty on the similarity could promote the exploitation of limited samples in few-shot optimization. In this work, we propose Uncertainty-Aware Few-Shot framework for image classification by modeling uncertainty of the similarities of query-support pairs and performing uncertainty-aware optimization. Particularly, we exploit such uncertainty by converting observed similarities to probabilistic representations and incorporate them to the loss for more effective optimization. In order to jointly consider the similarities between a query and the prototypes in a support set, a graph-based model is utilized to estimate the uncertainty of the pairs. Extensive experiments show our proposed method brings significant improvements on top of a strong baseline and achieves the state-of-the-art performance.

In this work, we present a simple yet powerful baseline for few-shot classification by emphasizing the importance of feature embedding. Specifically, we revisit the classical triplet network from deep metric learning, and extend it into a deep K-tuplet network for few-shot learning, utilizing the relationship among the input samples to learn a general representation learning via episode-training. Once trained, our network is able to extract discriminative features for unseen novel categories and can be seamlessly incorporated with a non-linear distance metric function to facilitate the few-shot classification. Our result on the miniImageNet benchmark outperforms other metric-based few-shot classification methods. More importantly, when evaluated on completely different datasets (Caltech-101, CUB-200, Stanford Dogs and Cars) using the model trained with miniImageNet, our method significantly outperforms prior methods, demonstrating its superior capability to generalize to unseen classes.

spans.quote: Few-shot learning is a challenging area of research that aims to learn new concepts with only a few labeled samples of data. Recent works based on metric-learning approaches leverage the meta-learning approach, which is encompassed by episodic tasks that make use a support (training) and query set (test) with the objective of learning a similarity comparison metric between those sets. Due to the lack of data, the learning process of the embedding network becomes an important part of the few-shot task. Previous works have addressed this problem using metric learning approaches, but the properties of the underlying latent space and the separability of the difference classes on it was not entirely enforced. In this work, we propose two different loss functions which consider the importance of the embedding vectors by looking at the intra-class and inter-class distance between the few data. The first loss function is the Proto-Triplet Loss, which is based on the original triplet loss with the modifications needed to better work on few-shot scenarios. The second loss function, which we dub ICNN loss is based on an inter and intra class nearest neighbors score, which help us to assess the quality of embeddings obtained from the trained network. Our results, obtained from a extensive experimental setup show a significant improvement in accuracy in the miniImagenNet benchmark compared to other metric-based few-shot learning methods by a margin of 2%, demonstrating the capability of these loss functions to allow the network to generalize better to previously unseen classes. In our experiments, we demonstrate competitive generalization capabilities to other domains, such as the Caltech CUB, Dogs and Cars datasets compared with the state of the art.

spans.quote: Few-shot learning is a challenging area of research that aims to learn new concepts with only a few labeled samples of data. Recent works based on metric-learning approaches leverage the meta-learning approach, which is encompassed by episodic tasks that make use a support (training) and query set (test) with the objective of learning a similarity comparison metric between those sets. Due to the lack of data, the learning process of the embedding network becomes an important part of the few-shot task. Previous works have addressed this problem using metric learning approaches, but the properties of the underlying latent space and the separability of the difference classes on it was not entirely enforced. In this work, we propose two different loss functions which consider the importance of the embedding vectors by looking at the intra-class and inter-class distance between the few data. The first loss function is the Proto-Triplet Loss, which is based on the original triplet loss with the modifications needed to better work on few-shot scenarios. The second loss function, which we dub ICNN loss is based on an inter and intra class nearest neighbors score, which help us to assess the quality of embeddings obtained from the trained network. Our results, obtained from a extensive experimental setup show a significant improvement in accuracy in the miniImagenNet benchmark compared to other metric-based few-shot learning methods by a margin of 2%, demonstrating the capability of these loss functions to allow the network to generalize better to previously unseen classes. In our experiments, we demonstrate competitive generalization capabilities to other domains, such as the Caltech CUB, Dogs and Cars datasets compared with the state of the art.

spans.quote: Few-shot learning is a challenging area of research that aims to learn new concepts with only a few labeled samples of data. Recent works based on metric-learning approaches leverage the meta-learning approach, which is encompassed by episodic tasks that make use a support (training) and query set (test) with the objective of learning a similarity comparison metric between those sets. Due to the lack of data, the learning process of the embedding network becomes an important part of the few-shot task. Previous works have addressed this problem using metric learning approaches, but the properties of the underlying latent space and the separability of the difference classes on it was not entirely enforced. In this work, we propose two different loss functions which consider the importance of the embedding vectors by looking at the intra-class and inter-class distance between the few data. The first loss function is the Proto-Triplet Loss, which is based on the original triplet loss with the modifications needed to better work on few-shot scenarios. The second loss function, which we dub ICNN loss is based on an inter and intra class nearest neighbors score, which help us to assess the quality of embeddings obtained from the trained network. Our results, obtained from a extensive experimental setup show a significant improvement in accuracy in the miniImagenNet benchmark compared to other metric-based few-shot learning methods by a margin of 2%, demonstrating the capability of these loss functions to allow the network to generalize better to previously unseen classes. In our experiments, we demonstrate competitive generalization capabilities to other domains, such as the Caltech CUB, Dogs and Cars datasets compared with the state of the art.

The goal of few-shot learning is to recognize new visual concepts with just a few amount of labeled samples in each class. Recent effective metric-based few-shot approaches employ neural networks to learn a feature similarity comparison between query and support examples. However, the importance of feature embedding, i.e., exploring the relationship among training samples, is neglected. In this work, we present a simple yet powerful baseline for few-shot classification by emphasizing the importance of feature embedding. Specifically, we revisit the classical triplet network from deep metric learning, and extend it into a deep K-tuplet network for few-shot learning, utilizing the relationship among the input samples to learn a general representation learning via episode-training. Once trained, our network is able to extract discriminative features for unseen novel categories and can be seamlessly incorporated with a non-linear distance metric function to facilitate the few-shot classification. Our result on the miniImageNet benchmark outperforms other metric-based few-shot classification methods. More importantly, when evaluated on completely different datasets (Caltech-101, CUB-200, Stanford Dogs and Cars) using the model trained with miniImageNet, our method significantly outperforms prior methods, demonstrating its superior capability to generalize to unseen classes.

Learning high quality class representations from few examples is a key problem in metric-learning approaches to few-shot learning. To accomplish this, we introduce a novel architecture where class representations are conditioned for each few-shot trial based on a target image. We also deviate from traditional metric-learning approaches by training a network to perform comparisons between classes rather than relying on a static metric comparison. This allows the network to decide what aspects of each class are important for the comparison at hand. We find that this flexible architecture works well in practice, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Caltech-UCSD birds fine-grained classification task.

In this paper, we propose a subspace representation learning (SRL) framework to tackle few-shot image classification tasks. It exploits a subspace in local CNN feature space to represent an image, and measures the similarity between two images according to a weighted subspace distance (WSD). When K images are available for each class, we develop two types of template subspaces to aggregate K-shot information: the prototypical subspace (PS) and the discriminative subspace (DS). Based on the SRL framework, we extend metric learning based techniques from vector to subspace representation. While most previous works adopted global vector representation, using subspace representation can effectively preserve the spatial structure, and diversity within an image. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the SRL framework on three public benchmark datasets: MiniImageNet, TieredImageNet and Caltech-UCSD Birds-200-2011 (CUB), and the experimental results illustrate competitive/superior performance of our method compared to the previous state-of-the-art.

In the context of few-shot classification, the goal is to train a classifier using a limited number of samples while maintaining satisfactory performance. However, traditional metric-based methods exhibit certain limitations in achieving this objective. These methods typically rely on a single distance value between the query feature and support feature, thereby overlooking the contribution of shallow features. To overcome this challenge, we propose a novel approach in this paper. Our approach involves utilizing a multi-output embedding network that maps samples into distinct feature spaces. The proposed method extracts feature vectors at different stages, enabling the model to capture both global and abstract features. By utilizing these diverse feature spaces, our model enhances its performance. Moreover, employing a self-attention mechanism improves the refinement of features at each stage, leading to even more robust representations and improved overall performance. Furthermore, assigning learnable weights to each stage significantly improved performance and results. We conducted comprehensive evaluations on the MiniImageNet and FC100 datasets, specifically in the 5-way 1-shot and 5-way 5-shot scenarios. Additionally, we performed cross-domain tasks across eight benchmark datasets, achieving high accuracy in the testing domains. These evaluations demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method in comparison to state-of-the-art approaches. https://github.com/FatemehAskari/MSENet

Few-shot image classification learns to recognize new categories from limited labelled data. Metric learning based approaches have been widely investigated, where a query sample is classified by finding the nearest prototype from the support set based on their feature similarities. A neural network has different uncertainties on its calculated similarities of different pairs. Understanding and modeling the uncertainty on the similarity could promote the exploitation of limited samples in few-shot optimization. In this work, we propose Uncertainty-Aware Few-Shot framework for image classification by modeling uncertainty of the similarities of query-support pairs and performing uncertainty-aware optimization. Particularly, we exploit such uncertainty by converting observed similarities to probabilistic representations and incorporate them to the loss for more effective optimization. In order to jointly consider the similarities between a query and the prototypes in a support set, a graph-based model is utilized to estimate the uncertainty of the pairs. Extensive experiments show our proposed method brings significant improvements on top of a strong baseline and achieves the state-of-the-art performance.

spans.quote: Few-shot image classification learns to recognize new categories from limited labelled data. Metric learning based approaches have been widely investigated, where a query sample is classified by finding the nearest prototype from the support set based on their feature similarities. A neural network has different uncertainties on its calculated similarities of different pairs. Understanding and modeling the uncertainty on the similarity could promote the exploitation of limited samples in few-shot optimization. In this work, we propose Uncertainty-Aware Few-Shot framework for image classification by modeling uncertainty of the similarities of query-support pairs and performing uncertainty-aware optimization. Particularly, we exploit such uncertainty by converting observed similarities to probabilistic representations and incorporate them to the loss for more effective optimization. In order to jointly consider the similarities between a query and the prototypes in a support set, a graph-based model is utilized to estimate the uncertainty of the pairs. Extensive experiments show our proposed method brings significant improvements on top of a strong baseline and achieves the state-of-the-art performance.

Few-shot image classification is a challenging problem that aims to achieve the human level of recognition based only on a small number of training images. One main solution to few-shot image classification is deep metric learning. These methods, by classifying unseen samples according to their distances to few seen samples in an embedding space learned by powerful deep neural networks, can avoid overfitting to few training images in few-shot image classification and have achieved the state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we provide an up-to-date review of deep metric learning methods for few-shot image classification from 2018 to 2022 and categorize them into three groups according to three stages of metric learning, namely learning feature embeddings, learning class representations, and learning distance measures. With this taxonomy, we identify the novelties of different methods and problems they face. We conclude this review with a discussion on current challenges and future trends in few-shot image classification.
